from solution import is_decimal


def test_issue_example_123_11():
    """Example asserts is_decimal('123.11') == True."""
    # digits after '.' in '123.11' = 2, 2 == 2 => True
    assert is_decimal('123.11') == True


def test_issue_zero_with_two_decimals():
    """Decimal with precision of 2 like '0.00' is True."""
    # digits after '.' in '0.00' = 2, 2 == 2 => True
    assert is_decimal('0.00') == True


def test_issue_one_decimal_place():
    """Precision of 2 needs exactly 2 digits so '123.1' is False."""
    # digits after '.' in '123.1' = 1, 1 != 2 => False
    assert is_decimal('123.1') == False


def test_issue_three_decimal_places():
    """Precision of 2 rejects 3 digits so '123.111' is False."""
    # digits after '.' in '123.111' = 3, 3 != 2 => False
    assert is_decimal('123.111') == False


def test_issue_integer_without_dot():
    """A decimal needs '.' so integer '123' is False."""
    # count of '.' in '123' = 0, 0 != 1 => False
    assert is_decimal('123') == False


def test_issue_empty_string():
    """Empty input is not a decimal with precision of 2."""
    # len('') == 0, 0 != 6 => False
    assert is_decimal('') == False


def test_issue_letters_only():
    """Letters 'abc' are not a decimal with precision of 2."""
    # digits after '.' = 0, 0 != 2 => False
    assert is_decimal('abc') == False


def test_issue_comma_separator():
    """Decimal separator must be '.' so '123,11' is False."""
    # count of '.' in '123,11' = 0, 0 != 1 => False
    assert is_decimal('123,11') == False


def test_issue_trailing_letter():
    """Whole string must match so '123.11a' is False."""
    # len('123.11a') = 7, 7 != 6 => False
    assert is_decimal('123.11a') == False


def test_issue_leading_space():
    """Whole string must match so ' 123.11' is False."""
    # len(' 123.11') = 7, 7 != 6 => False
    assert is_decimal(' 123.11') == False


def test_contract_returns_bool_on_valid():
    """Return value supports '== True' so valid input returns bool."""
    # digits after '.' in '123.11' = 2, 2 == 2 => True and type is bool
    assert isinstance(is_decimal('123.11'), bool) == True


def test_contract_returns_bool_on_invalid():
    """Return value supports '== False' so invalid input returns bool."""
    # digits after '.' in 'abc' = 0, 0 != 2 => False and type is bool
    assert isinstance(is_decimal('abc'), bool) == True
